records.sourceAnchor: SC eligibility, INR 5 lakh income ceiling, channel route, 90% project-cost boundary, product-specific ceilings/rates/repayment and separate support activities
observations: The current NSFDC FAQ identifies NSFDC as a Government public-sector undertaking under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and states that loan beneficiaries must belong to the Scheduled Caste community and have annual family income from all sources not exceeding INR 5 lakh, effective 7 January 2026 and subject to amendment.

Applicants cannot apply directly to NSFDC for a loan. Applications must be routed through authorized State Channelizing Agencies or other Channelizing Agencies, using PM-SURAJ where available or the relevant offline channel partner route.

The current FAQ states that NSFDC provides up to 90% of project cost across its credit schemes. Product-specific project cost, maximum loan, interest, moratorium and repayment terms must remain separate.

The current FAQ describes MFS for projects up to INR 1.40 lakh with maximum loan INR 1.25 lakh at 6.5% p.a. and repayment within 3 years including a 3-month moratorium; AMY covers the same project-cost boundary and maximum loan at 15% p.a. with the same repayment period.

The current FAQ describes Term Loan for projects above INR 1.40 lakh and up to INR 50 lakh, maximum loan INR 45 lakh at 8% p.a., repayment within 7 years including a 6-month moratorium, extended to 12 months for plantation and construction activities.

The current FAQ describes Udyam Nidhi for projects up to INR 5 lakh, maximum loan INR 4.50 lakh, with 13% beneficiary interest through cooperative societies/banks and 15% through Small Finance Banks, repayable within 5 years including a 3-month moratorium.

Partnership firms and cooperative societies may apply when all members belong to the Scheduled Caste community and each member satisfies the applicable INR 5 lakh income threshold. Skill-development and market-linkage support are separate activities and must not be added to loan value.

The route remains concessional channel finance, not a grant or guaranteed sanction. UdyamVeda may prepare and explain the checklist but must not submit as the applicant, collect OTPs or represent itself as NSFDC or a channel partner.

Confirm product-specific eligibility, legal/viable activity definitions, entity-form rules and the treatment of partnerships and cooperatives.
Keep MFS, AMY, Term Loan and Udyam Nidhi as separate product tracks; do not combine loan ceilings or add training/market-support values to credit.
Obtain human reviewer approval for source, eligibility, benefit, application, window, fine print, amendment, current terms and factual accuracy before publication.
